[0] everyday_reading (E): Folk meaning: 'reverse every element' suggests one swap per position, so the loop runs over all n positions. Java rule: each exchange moves two elements, so n/2 exchanges (i < N/2) reverse the array, and n exchanges reverse it twice, restoring the original.
[1] misconception (M) -> ReverseFullLength: wrong rule: Reversing an array needs a swap for every one of the n positions. Right rule: Swapping for i < n/2 is enough; going to n undoes the reversal.
[2] inconsistent_trace (T) -> ReverseFullLength: Points to LT: for i from 0 while i < N/2, save a[i] in temp, copy a[N-1-i] to a[i], and copy temp to a[N-1-i]. Inconsistent application: the trace exchanges a mirror pair on some passes but only copies one way on others, or computes the mirror with an updated i. (here mixing in: "Reversing an array needs a swap for every one of the n positions")
[3] misconception (M) -> OffByOneBound: wrong rule: < vs <= and 0..n vs 0..n-1 are interchangeable. Right rule: The mirror of a[i] is a[N-1-i] (not a[N-i]), and the loop runs while i < N/2.

[0] names_the_element (N): Identity: in-place reversal rearranges an array so that a[i] and a[N-1-i] trade places for every i, without a second array.
[1] states_the_rule (S): Declarative: for (int i = 0; i < N/2; i++) { temp = b[i]; b[i] = b[N-1-i]; b[N-1-i] = temp; }.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): Sequencing: pass i exchanges the i-th pair from the outside in: (0, N-1), (1, N-2), ... For odd N the middle element is never touched, because N/2 rounds down.
[1] output_prediction (OP): Result: {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} becomes {5, 4, 3, 2, 1} with the same length and the same values.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): State transition: each pass changes exactly two elements, a[i] and a[N-1-i] (plus temp); other elements and N are unchanged.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): Reversal is a loop of exchanges a[i] <-> a[N-1-i], so it inherits the exchange idiom and its temporary variable.
[1] relation_to_neighbour (R): Reversal traverses only the first half (i < N/2) while indexing the second half through the mirror index.
[2] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Plan/role: a two-ended mirror-swap plan in which the array plays the role of an organizer, its elements rearranged in place.

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> ReverseFullLength: Conservation: the multiset of values is preserved (only exchanges are used). Reversal is its own inverse: reversing twice, or running the loop to N instead of N/2, gives back the original order.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Applicability: reverse in place when the original order is no longer needed and memory matters. When the original must be kept, copy into a new array (b[N-1-i] = a[i]) or just traverse backwards.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Only the first half is traversed. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: the loop runs i < N, so every pair is swapped twice and the array ends unchanged
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: The mirror index is N-1-i. Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: the mirror is written a[N-i], which is a[N] at i = 0 (ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException)
[4] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: The exchange needs a temporary variable. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: a[i] = a[N-1-i]; a[N-1-i] = a[i]; leaves the array a palindrome of its second half

Reversal exchanges a[i] with a[N-1-i] for each i in the first half of the array.
Reversal traverses only the first half of the array (i < N/2), exchanging each a[i] with its mirror a[N-1-i].
Reversal pairs a[i] with a[a.length-1-i], counting back from the last index a.length-1.
